method: In Miha's class, we read the article "Criptech and the Art of Access" by Vanessa Chang and Lindsey D. Felt. Miha had us each read a paragraph, and we worked through the text together. To be honest, I didn't understand the meaning of many words at first, though I managed to figure them out by looking them up on Google (or Baidu). Even then, I still didn't quite grasp everything—haha—but AI-generated annotations helped explain the concepts in simpler terms.
conclusion_future_work:
Week Project：
I read the article 《Criptech and the Art of Access》. Afterward, Miha asked me to choose two or three words; personally, I was drawn to "integrated access" and"Creative access".
Integrated Access：It typically emphasizes integrating accessibility needs into the entire design, space, or activity, rather than adding assistive measures for specific individuals as an afterthought.Simply put: take the needs of different people into account from the very beginning, and enable everyone to participate.
Creative access：The specific meaning of this term depends heavily on context, but it may refer to:
- Enabling broader participation in creation: Providing opportunities for people to create, regardless of their physical abilities, financial circumstances, or technical skills.
- Achieving accessibility through creative means: Using interactive installations, games, or visual design to make information easier for diverse audiences to understand.
- Accessing creative resources: Making it easier for people to engage with art, design, creative tools, or cultural activities.
In simple terms: giving more people the chance to access creativity and participate in the creative process, or using creative design to remove barriers to participation.
Miha also asked us to discuss two or three of the works featured in the article—focusing on the artworks themselves rather than our personal reactions—and I chose
1. *did not feel low, was sleeping* (2022).
*did not feel low, was sleeping* (2022) is a collaborative artwork by Laura Forlano and artist Itziar Barrio. The piece utilizes raw data from Forlano’s smart insulin pump and sensory system—data linked to her experience living with type 1 diabetes. It explores how personal health data is generated and examines the ways in which people care for machines designed to care for them.
2.Unseen Sound
Unseen Sound by Andy Slater is an immersive virtual environment that can be navigated through sound. Sonic text descriptions are the only visual elements of the work. Instead of relying on conventional visual navigation, the work uses sound and text-based descriptions as the main ways to explore the virtual environment.
3.TOUCH
TOUCH by Nat Decker is an immersive artwork created on the New Art City platform. It is designed for both web browsers and virtual reality headsets. The work uses an immersive digital environment and explores how accessibility can change the way creative technologies function.
results_discussion: I completed all of Miha's assignments, noting down the artworks that interested me and the words I didn't understand; finally, I previewed the article she sent me, and everything is now ready.
